## Table of Trial Solutions for the Method of Undetermined Coefficients

We can choose an *Ansatz* to the particular solution based on the following table:

```{=latex}
\begin{center}
{\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
\begin{tabular}{|l|l|l|}
\hline
 & $f(t)$ & $y_p$ \\ \hline
\small{Constant} & C & $A_0$ \\ \hline
\small{$n$th order polynomial} & $P_n(t) = P_nt^n + P_{n-1} t^{n-1} + \cdots + P_0$ & $A_n(t) = A_nt^n + A_{n-1}t^{n-1} + \cdots + A_0$ \\ \hline
\small{Exponential} & $e^{\alpha t}$ & $A_0e^{\alpha t}$ \\ \hline
\small{Trigonometric} & $\cos{(\beta t)}$, $\sin{(\beta t)}$, or $\cos{(\beta t)} + \sin{(\beta t)}$  & $A_0\cos{(\beta t)}+B_0\sin{(\beta t)}$ \\ \hline
\small{Polynomial} $\times$ Exponential & $P_n(t)e^{\alpha t}$ & $A_n(t)e^{\alpha t}$ \\ \hline
\small{Polynomial $\times$ Trigonometric} & $P_n(t)\cos{(\beta t)} + Q_n(t)\sin{(\beta t)}$ & $A_n(t)\cos{(\beta t)}+B_n(t)\sin{(\beta t)}$ \\ \hline
\small{Exponential $\times$ Trigonometric} & $e^{\alpha t}\cos{(\beta t)} + e^{\alpha t}\sin{(\beta t)}$ & $A_0e^{\alpha t}\cos{(\beta t)} + B_0e^{\alpha t}\sin{(\beta t)}$ \\ \hline
\end{tabular}
}
\end{center}
```

\

*Note: If some terms of $y_p$ are found in $y_h(t)$ (i.e. such terms are the same as the homogeneous solution), multiply the expression for $y_p(t)$ by $t$ (or, if necessary, by $t^2$) to eliminate the duplication.*
